result.title: Physics-Informed but Not Physics-Consistent: Error Geometry and Subspace Projection for Neural AC Power Flow
result.summary: Recent neural power-flow solvers, including emerging foundation models, achieve accurate voltage predictions, yet such accuracy does not necessarily imply physically consistent solutions. Even small complex voltage errors can yield large AC power-balance residuals. We study this accuracy-consistency gap across PIGNN-GC, GridSFM, gridfm-graphkit, and LUMINA on realistic 2224-bus Great Britain network (GBnetwork) scenarios, with cross-grid evaluation of GridSFM over 31 systems. Using a singular value decomposition (SVD) basis fitted to training AC power-flow solutions, we find that neural prediction errors contain substantial components outside the dominant solution subspace. To address this mismatch, calibrated solution-subspace projection (CSP) suppresses off-subspace prediction components after train-only bias calibration, reducing Mean PB by 67.0%, 37.8%, 40.5%, and 68.9% for PIGNN-GC, GridSFM, gridfm-graphkit, and LUMINA, respectively, relative to calibrated predictions, while improving voltage-magnitude accuracy in all four models. These results identify output-error geometry as an important factor in physics-consistent neural AC power flow. Code: https://github.com/Kimchangheon/neural-acpf-error-geometry

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究神经潮流求解器的「精度—物理一致性」差距，用 SVD 拟合同解子空间，发现预测误差大量落在主导子空间之外，并提出校准子空间投影（CSP）抑制子空间外分量，在四个模型上大幅降低功率平衡残差。
AI.relevance_reason: 误差几何与子空间投影的思路可能启发 LVR 中 latent 状态的质量诊断：可核查视觉证据是否被投影到任务相关子空间、以及「表示准确但推理不一致」的类似失败模式。
